items.title: 13.1 Volatility of chlorine, bromine and iodine (yeh kitni jaldi bhaap banti hain) (Roman Urdu)

source_refs.note: Roman Urdu explanation of topic 13.1, printed page 293.

blocks.text: Chlorine room temperature par bohat volatile (jaldi bhaap ya gas ban kar urne wali) hai aur hawa mein jaldi phail jati hai. Bromine liquid hai; yeh chlorine se kam volatile hai magar iodine se zyada. Room temperature par yeh aasani se bhaap ban kar toxic (zehreele) dhuen chhorti hai. Teenon mein iodine sab se kam volatile hai: room temperature par is ki solid state chlorine aur bromine ke muqable mein kam volatility dikhati hai. Aam taur par volatility chlorine se iodine tak kam hoti jati hai. Wajah: group mein neeche jate hue molecular mass barhta hai, bahar wale shell ka size barhta hai, aur molecules ke darmiyan intermolecular forces (London dispersion forces) strong (mazboot) hoti jati hain.

blocks.title: Kitab ki ghalti
blocks.text: Kitab likhti hai “Chlorine being a liquid”, yani chlorine liquid hai. Yeh ghalat hai: room temperature par chlorine gas hai (bromine liquid aur iodine solid hai). Isi liye chlorine teenon mein sab se zyada volatile hai.

blocks.title: Interesting Information (dilchasp maloomat)
blocks.text: Bromine liquid room temperature par aasani se bhaap ban kar orange (narangi) rang ki bhaap chhorti hai. Is ki boo bohat teez aur buri hai. Is ka naam Greek lafz “bromos” se hai, jis ka matlab hai “stench” (badboo).

blocks.prompt: Volatility chlorine se iodine tak kyun kam hoti hai?
blocks.explanation: Neeche jate hue molecules bare aur bhaari hote hain, aur un ke darmiyan London dispersion forces strong hoti hain. Molecules ko ek doosre se alag kar ke gas banane ke liye zyada energy chahiye, is liye volatility kam hoti hai: Cl₂ (gas) > Br₂ (liquid) > I₂ (solid).

items: Wajah: neeche jate hue molecular mass, size aur London dispersion forces barhti hain.
Kitab ki ghalti: chlorine liquid nahi, gas hai.
